newsitem.title: GERMANY: Santer sees prompt EMU start with majority of states.
newsitem.headline: Santer sees prompt EMU start with majority of states.

text.p: European Commission President Jacques Santer said on Wednesday he was confident economic and monetary union (EMU) would begin on time with a majority of European Union member states in the starting lineup.
"I am very optimistic that the euro will come on January 1, 1999 with a pleasing majority of countries," Santer told reporters during a visit to Bonn.

German politics have recently been dominated by a heated debate over whether Bonn can meet the strict fiscal criteria to join EMU, and Chancellor Helmut Kohl has now pledged to hit exactly the Maastricht treaty budget deficit goal of three percent of GDP.

Santer said, however, that the debate was not helpful and that he did not want to encourage speculation over who will fulfil the criteria before government leaders decide next year which EU members should join the single currency.

"I believe, as the chancellor has said, that every member state should do its own homework now, and then heads of government will make their decision on the basis of reports from the European Commission and the European Monetary Institute," Santer said.
"We should work towards that, and we should not start any speculation. That leads only to annoyance or even uncertainty."
Santer was in Bonn to discuss the impact of the EU's planned eastward enlargement in the next century and regional aid policy with the premiers of Germany's 16 federal states.
He said the commission had proposed that the states from the formerly-communist east Germany could expect to remain in the highest aid category when subsidy policy comes up for review in 1999.
